changes: Added the parallel-decomposition gate CONFIG layer (spec §4.7): resolveParallelGate(raw, profileDefault) in audit-config.ts — a thin total wrapper over readParallelGateFields that validates a nested {mode,maxConcurrentReview,broadGlobBlocks} object field-by-field with per-field warn+fallback, plus per-profile defaults (light advise/2/false, balanced advise/3/false, strict block/4/true) wired into resolveAuditConfig. Hardened to be provably total (Object.hasOwn presence, describeInvalidValue used for every untrusted-input rendering incl. the catch err). New hermetic 82-assertion smoke; spec §4.7 and lattice.config.json updated.
usage: Operators set parallelGate in .lattice/audit-config.json (per-field override over profile defaults); resolveAuditConfig(profile, projectRoot).parallelGate returns the resolved {mode,maxConcurrentReview,broadGlobBlocks}. mode 'off' is the reversible escape hatch; any present-but-invalid value warns and falls back without ever crashing the gate.
expectedOutcome: lattice validate runs all 9 commands green, including 'parallel-gate-config smoke passed: 82 assertions'. resolveParallelGate never throws for any input and never silently promotes a default to 'block'.
actualTranscript: lattice validate: 9/9 commands green; parallel-gate-config-smoke.js prints 'parallel-gate-config smoke passed: 82 assertions' (exit 0). Full multi-round genuine dual-host review (Claude lanes + Codex host-2) drove findings F-001..F-026 to resolution; rounds 6 and 7 both returned PASS from Codex and all Claude lanes.
outcomeDiff: none — expected and actual match: 82 assertions pass, validate green, totality and per-profile defaults confirmed by both hosts.
limitations: The exotic-input hardening (bigint/circular/revoked-Proxy/hostile-trap) is defense-in-depth beyond the JSON-config contract (config always comes from JSON.parse, so those values are unreachable in production); it honors the function's exported never-throw contract. The broad outer try/catch is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (F-025 accepted_risk).
pitfalls: Presence MUST use Object.hasOwn, not 'key in r' (prototype-chain leak silently promotes defaults to block). Every rendering of untrusted input must go through describeInvalidValue (JSON.stringify/instanceof/String/toString all throw on exotic values). Sub-fields must be read ONCE into a const before validate+assign to avoid a hostile-getter guard/assign TOCTOU.
